question.question: Does automatic joint-configuration exit retain an implementation-owned continuation when the application-completion attempt is rejected during leadership transfer and the transfer later times out with the same leader, a live joint quorum, and no unrelated proposals?
question.importance: A joint configuration can remain effective after the requested implicit transition should finalize, continuing to require the outgoing quorum and preventing ordinary subsequent membership changes. This is a scoped membership progress responsibility, not a demonstrated consensus safety violation.
contexts: Synchronous RawNode Ready/Advance
JointImplicit change
Leader remains eligible in both configurations
Transfer fails because its emitted TimeoutNow is lost; all subsequent ordinary messages and storage/application work delivered
event_paths: Committed implicit change -> ApplyConfChange -> TransferLeader -> Advance -> automatic proposal rejected -> timer aborts transfer -> heartbeat/Ready service without new application proposals

supporting_behavior_ids.B-form: Commits the original configuration and determines whether later automatic exit enters the log.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-persist: Ready storage and Advance ordering ensures the overlap does not fabricate application or durability completion.

Node.ProposeConfChange generally permits caller proposals to be dropped, but JointImplicit explicitly assigns the exit proposal to Raft; JointExplicit assigns it to the caller.
The existing auto-leave test covers leadership loss and recovery with new application work, not a failed transfer leaving the same leader idle.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities

grounding.derivation: The public ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit contract assigns automatic exit by proposing a zero configuration change to Raft; ConfState.AutoLeave specifies finalization when safe. EnterJoint implements that selection. appliedTo explicitly acknowledges rejection during transfer and describes retry on later advance. The general caller-retry contract for dropped Propose/ProposeConfChange calls does not transfer ownership of this library-generated exit to the caller, especially because JointExplicit separately exposes that choice. The requirement concerns eventual implementation-owned continuation under continuing duties, not completion within an invented tick bound.
grounding.applicability: Implicit-joint change already committed/applied, same eligible leader remains, transfer timeout removes the temporary proposal-rejection guard, and both quorums and caller services remain available.
alternatives: Later unrelated proposal or leadership replacement can rescue progress; these are not required caller steps under the selected implicit-joint interface.

claims.description: With ReadOnlySafe, a caller using a fresh request context and a matching returned ReadState, and waiting until local application is strictly beyond its index, must not complete a read that omits a write completed before that read invocation when there is no intervening overwriting write. This remains required when a voter is legally demoted to a learner with StepDownOnRemoval disabled.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities

grounding.derivation: ReadOnlySafe promises linearizability; Node.ReadIndex/Ready specify a returned matching-context barrier and the local application threshold. A completed read after a completed write must include that write if no later write changes it. The construction honors the stricter literal applied>index wording. The demoted replica remains a learner, not a stopped removed member. StepDownOnRemoval is optional and its false setting has no documented reduction of ReadOnlySafe. Ready says SoftState need not be consumed, so adding caller-side term invalidation would introduce an extra duty absent from the supplied API.
grounding.applicability: The learner receives its barrier locally before learning the higher term, then finishes application of a real prefix beyond the barrier while the newer completed write is still undelivered.
alternatives: StepDownOnRemoval=true prevents this source path in the diagnostic control.
Greater applied index alone does not fix a barrier already below a write completed before the read invocation.

materials.text:
```

After creating a Node, the user has a few responsibilities:

First, read from the Node.Ready() channel and process the updates it contains. These steps may be performed in parallel, except as noted in step 2.

1. Write Entries, HardState and Snapshot to persistent storage in order, i.e. Entries first, then HardState and Snapshot if they are not empty. If persistent storage supports atomic writes then all of them can be written together. Note that when writing an Entry with Index i, any previously-persisted entries with Index >= i must be discarded.

2. Send all Messages to the nodes named in the To field. It is important that no messages be sent until the latest HardState has been persisted to disk, and all Entries written by any previous Ready batch (Messages may be sent while entries from the same batch are being persisted). To reduce the I/O latency, an optimization can be applied to make leader write to disk in parallel with its followers (as explained at section 10.2.1 in Raft thesis). If any Message has type MsgSnap, call Node.ReportSnapshot() after it has been sent (these messages may be large). Note: Marshalling messages is not thread-safe; it is important to make sure that no new entries are persisted while marshalling. The easiest way to achieve this is to serialise the messages directly inside the main raft loop.

3. Apply Snapshot (if any) and CommittedEntries to the state machine. If any committed Entry has Type EntryConfChange, call Node.ApplyConfChange() to apply it to the node. The configuration change may be cancelled at this point by setting the NodeID field to zero before calling ApplyConfChange (but ApplyConfChange must be called one way or the other, and the decision to cancel must be based solely on the state machine and not external information such as the observed health of the node).

4. Call Node.Advance() to signal readiness for the next batch of updates. This may be done at any time after step 1, although all updates must be processed in the order they were returned by Ready.

Second, all persisted log entries must be made available via an implementation of the Storage interface. The provided MemoryStorage type can be used for this (if repopulating its state upon a restart), or a custom disk-backed implementation can be supplied.

Third, after receiving a message from another node, pass it to Node.Step:

```go
	func recvRaftRPC(ctx context.Context, m raftpb.Message) {
		n.Step(ctx, m)
	}
```

Finally, call `Node.Tick()` at regular intervals (probably via a `time.Ticker`). Raft has two important timeouts: heartbeat and the election timeout. However, internally to the raft package time is represented by an abstract "tick".

The total state machine handling loop will look something like this:

```go
  for {
    select {
    case <-s.Ticker:
      n.Tick()
    case rd := <-s.Node.Ready():
      saveToStorage(rd.HardState, rd.Entries, rd.Snapshot)
      send(rd.Messages)
      if !raft.IsEmptySnap(rd.Snapshot) {
        processSnapshot(rd.Snapshot)
      }
      for _, entry := range rd.CommittedEntries {
        process(entry)
        if entry.Type == raftpb.EntryConfChange {
          var cc raftpb.ConfChange
          cc.Unmarshal(entry.Data)
          s.Node.ApplyConfChange(cc)
        }
      }
      s.Node.Advance()
    case <-s.done:
      return
    }
  }
```

To propose changes to the state machine from the node to take application data, serialize it into a byte slice and call:

```go
	n.Propose(ctx, data)
```

If the proposal is committed, data will appear in committed entries with type raftpb.EntryNormal. There is no guarantee that a proposed command will be committed; the command may have to be reproposed after a timeout.

To add or remove node in a cluster, build ConfChange struct 'cc' and call:

```go

No message bytes or target state are altered.
In-memory stable storage models successful persistence, without crashes.
Application is a deterministic one-register state machine; all reads and mutations occur on the same goroutine.

plan_uncertainties: Scope is the demonstrated retained-learner, optional-stepdown-false history; other membership and storage modes are not covered.
Formal applicability and correspondence must be reviewed against actual execution and generated wire events.

boundaries: Caller serving before the documented application boundary.
StepDownOnRemoval=true as a formal scenario; it is a diagnostic control.

items.rationale:
Reviewed fixed artifact c52895a53e47457d84e514dbfc529729 v1, its retained harness and plan, claim/bindings v1, and raw execution 90b52d071c5c4272b13d717b4bfd1160. The obligation applies because JointImplicit explicitly makes Raft propose the zero change and AutoLeave promises final configuration when safe; JointExplicit separately requires a caller proposal. The general dropped-client-proposal retry clause does not make an unrelated new command a required continuation for this internal exit.

History and caller duties: all three RawNodes are created with actual MemoryStorage and Bootstrap peers 1,2,3; Ready processing persists entries and HardState before any network delivery, applies configuration entries in order, and calls Advance. Campaign is exercised normally and the initial term-2 no-op is fully applied before the implicit removal of voter 3. The joint entry is generated, replicated and committed at index 5. The hook invokes public TransferLeader(2) after ApplyConfChange of that entry and before Advance of the same Ready; these are serialized public operations and no contract excludes that overlap. This is after Ready internally called acceptReady, so its prohibition on intervening mutation between readyWithoutAccept and acceptReady is respected. The normal implementation generates TimeoutNow and the network policy drops exactly one such message during the initial drain. It never drops a local durability/application response; the loss policy is then disabled. All subsequent node ticks, queued messages and Ready work are serviced. Normal no-op entries need no state-machine data effect; the membership-changing entries are actually applied. No call substitutes a fabricated vote, append reply, committed index or completion.

Observed correlation: overlap=true is a preselected input; control overlap=false is excluded before matching prerequisites. The operation label is independent of the compared state. There is one matching admitted operation, its change index and term are bound to the settled prerequisite, and one independent continuation_result. Raw logs show admission at committed index 5 with AutoLeave=true and transferee=2; settlement shows applied=committed=last=5, same leader and term 2, transferee=0, one lost TimeoutNow and no queue/Ready work. The monitor recorded matched prerequisites and no parsing errors. Control events share the operation label but cannot match the overlap=true prerequisite conditions; no result is selected from that control.

Oracle and recurrence: the assertion requires forbidden_cycle=false. Its observed true value is a conjunction computed from actual target state and the executed schedule, not from the expected answer. I independently parsed the retained raw cycle_start and cycle_end strings: both 18,121-character structural snapshots are equal. They include every reflected RawNode, raft, log, unstable, MemoryStorage, tracker, per-peer inflight/buffer, read queue, stored response, timer and function identity field, including unexported fields, slice nilness/capacity and the transport queue. All three nodes have committed=applied=applying=5, zero applying bytes and no paused application. All outgoing/deferred message slices and stepsOnAdvance are empty. Leader electionElapsed and heartbeatElapsed are zero at both ends; followers' election timers are also zero, with captured randomized deadlines 16,16,12 for nodes 1,2,3. The cycle delivered 20 MsgHeartbeat and 20 MsgHeartbeatResp, no other type, retained joint state throughout, and reached a drained boundary.

Closure and observation ownership: one test goroutine performs all target calls and sampling; no Node run goroutine, storage worker, pending Ready or application callback exists. The fixed input schedule ticks nodes 1,2,3 then drains the FIFO until quiescence, repeated ten times. Those same inputs can be repeated from the equal state. Driver counters and output timestamps do not influence protocol inputs. Snapshot omissions are specifically the logger sinks and MemoryStorage.callStats. Reading the storage methods and all callStats uses establishes increment-only diagnostic accounting; default logger writes diagnostics, and the build assertion plus state_trace_nop establishes no active tracing callback. Logger state and crypto randomness cannot supply a missing continuation: heartbeat handling resets follower election timers, the active leader satisfies quorum checks, no election/role-reset path runs in this suffix, and random draws occur only in resetRandomizedElectionTimeout. Captured function code identities are sufficient here because tick/step receiver objects are the same instances and their data is included; no closure replacement happens. Thus this is a repeatable reliable execution with available quorums, not a deadline inferred from thirty ticks.

Causal account and contrary evidence: appliedTo tries the automatic proposal while leadTransferee is set; stepLeader rejects proposals during transfer. tickHeartbeat aborts transfer but abortLeaderTransfer only clears the field. Subsequent heartbeat-only Ready batches contain no committed entries, so acceptReady queues no MsgStorageApplyResp and Advance never calls appliedTo again. This explains the missing continuation. The fixed control left joint at index 6. The later ordinary-proposal diagnostic caused application and exit at index 7. Both are retained and show that application or a future leader/no-op can rescue progress; neither is a caller duty needed to finalize an already-applied implicit transition. This review supports the scoped implementation discrepancy, not a broader safety or deployment availability conclusion.
items.report_title: 领导权转移超时后，自动退出联合配置丢失后续触发
items.report_answer: 隐式联合配置在索引 5 应用时与领导权转移重叠，转移超时后仍停留在联合状态。正式执行记录了处理 20 次心跳及 20 次回复后协议状态完全重复、无待处理工作；追加普通提案才触发退出。该结果限定于自动配置收尾的进展责任，不表示共识安全性被破坏。
limitations: One synchronous RawNode transfer-overlap history; asynchronous storage and other configuration histories are not tested.
The repeated-cycle argument abstracts diagnostic counters and logger state only; it assumes continuing memory/storage availability and the selected reliable input schedule.
No numerical deadline, state-machine safety failure, external client outage or whole-deployment consequence is established.
